We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=3 & \,⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 3\,\text{d}x=3x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{2}(3x)-\int (3x)(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{2}-\int 6\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int 6\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x) & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=6 & \,⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 6\,\text{d}x=6x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)(6x)-\int (6x)(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-\int 6\,\text{d}x \\  & =6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-6x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{2}\,\text{d}x & =3x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{2}-\int 6\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{2}-(6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)-6x+D) \\  & =3x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{2}-6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)+6x-D \\  & =3x((\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)+2)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/3}^{e/3}3(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{2}\text{d}x & ={[3x((\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x))^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)+2)]}_{1/3}^{e/3} \\  & =[3(\frac{e}{3})({(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3\cdot \frac{e}{3}))}^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3\cdot \frac{e}{3})+2)]-[3(\frac{1}{3})({(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3\cdot \frac{1}{3}))}^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(3\cdot \frac{1}{3})+2)] \\  & =[e((\operatorname{ln}⁡e)^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡e+2)]-[1((\operatorname{ln}⁡1)^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡1+2)] \\  & =[e(1-2+2)]-[1(0-0+2)] \\  & =e-2\end{aligned}
$$
